Monday, May 18, 2020  7:00 PM  Teleconference

Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Park and Activities Commission Members will be
participating via teleconference.

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and available for viewing.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
870 4036 9262 , Meeting Password: 070197. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in
option from a phone line.)

- Public correspondence may be emailed to the Cynthia Morquecho, Community Services Supervisor at
cynthiam@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded
to the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an
“eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp
page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen
by the public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 870 4036 9262 , Meeting Password: 070197.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MAY 18, 2020

  The Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at 7:02
  p.m. on the Zoom Chat format by CHAIR PERSICHINA.

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR PERSICHINA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Perichina, Pope,  Bain,  Romanelli,  Ciarolla,
  McCormick, Retz

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  None

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager (ACM)
  Mike Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  Cynthia Morquecho, Comm. Services Supervisor
  Daniel A-Haja, Community Services Coordinator

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED DRAFT MINUTES OF APRIL 20,
  2020

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted an update to the minutes regarding the Armenian Plaque.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL
  20, 2020 AS REVISED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A. HIGHRIDGE PARK MURAL PROJECT

DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
MAY 18, 2020
   COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided a brief overview per
  the agenda material.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if the large mural would be on the garage or can be moved.
  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO replied that the larger mural would be on the back side of
  the shed facing the street but can be moved to the garage door but would be more hidden
  from public view. CHAIR PERISCHINA asked the Commission if they approve of the
  location of the larger mural. COMMISSIONER RETZ liked original location of the mural.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if the cost of the bulletin mural was per side.
  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO replied that was correct and that if both sides were desired
  then it would be double the cost.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the bulletin board was only used by the City.
  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO replied that the bulletin board is used by the public as a
  community board and for City messages but is monitored by the City. COMMISSIONER
  BAIN stated that since it was repainted, the board has not been in use. SUPERVISOR
  MORQUECHO noted that the board is under-utilized. SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH
  noted the bulletin board was repainted about 6 or 7 months ago along with the restroom
  repainting. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if both sides of the bulletin board will
  be painted or whether one side will be left for community messages. He pointed out
  possibility of wear and tear on the mural over time. SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO replied
  that room would be made for the postings.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the restroom mural square footage was about the
  size of the tennis practice wall due to having past experience with this. SUPERVISOR
  MORQUECHO replied that the pricing comes from the $13 per square foot quote provided
  by the artist, which is comparable to other Cities.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if all three murals are approved by the Commission.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated the location of the restroom mural would be out of view
  from most of the park and would be unnecessary. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI and
  CHAIR PERSICHINA agreed.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK stated that if the bulletin board was not being used as
  much after the remodeling, that the space could be used for a park bench.
  SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH responded that the bulletin board does get plenty of
  use from residents as a Lost & Found board and is a good place to promote the City’s
  special events.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested posting sign that label the bulletin board so that people
  would know what the structure was. She added that if the bulletin board portion should not
  be part of the mural so as not to encourage defacing the artwork. She suggested one side
  for a mural and another labeled as a community message board.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA asked the Commission to confirm only approving two mural
  locations. ALL COMMISSIONERS agreed to two mural locations.

DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
MAY 18, 2020
   CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if the cost was agreeable to the Commission.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that the cost was in line with the last project, but
  that during the last project the end date was under-estimated by a few months. He also
  noted the unexpected scaffolding cost associated with the Ernie Howlett mural which
  increased the initial cost of the project.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if the Commission is to approve the attached
  images for the mural. SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO replied that the artist is open to
  direction from the Commission. CHAIR PERSICHINA stated that this was also done with
  the last mural for the City. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI agreed with the method used
  for the last mural of Commission approval. VICE CHAIR POPE stated that Highridge is a
  different type of park and that the Nature aspect of the mural is better suited for Highridge.
  All Commissioners approved the large mural placed on the back wall of the garage.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked what the creature was at the bottom center of the mural.
  ARTIST MARIANNA DESALLES responded that the creature was a depiction of a
  mountain lion but could be removed or replaced. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if all the
  animals depicted were local to the area as she did not think the mountain lion was a local
  animal. DESALLES responded that the mountain lion could be removed.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested approving which of the two designs they would like for
  the murals so as to only make one motion. DESALLES added the bulletin mural’s design
  could include more hexagons to simulate a beehive. SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH
  added the middle portion of the bulletin board could be made of hexagonal-shaped cork
  to incorporate the mural with the board. The Commission was in agreement with both
  proposed pictures on either side of the bulletin. COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if having
  the two sides of the building would be double the original quote of $424. DESALLES
  answered yes. CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if it would still be within budget. DESALLES
  responded affirmatively. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked to also have the bulletin board
  labeled for the public to know they could place postings as well.

  VICE CHAIR POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to:

  APPROVE STAFF RECOMMENDATION OF USING THE GARAGE WALL AND BOTH
  SIDES OF THE BULLETIN BOARD FOR PROPOSED MURALS AS PRESENTED
  WITHIN THE PROPOSED BUDGET.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA REQUESTED A ROLL CALL:

  AYES: Persichina, Pope, Ciarolla, Bain, McCormick, Retz, & Romanelli
  NAYES: None
  ABSENT : None

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  B. REVISIONS TO PARK REGULATIONS MUNICIPAL CODE

  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA provided a brief overview per the
  agenda material.

DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
MAY 18, 2020
   COMMISSIONER RETZ noted section 12.24.130 which talks about park hours, should
  include City sponsored events.  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR
  MORQUECHO responded that staff will work with the City Attorney to include that
  information.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR POPE to:

  APPROVE STAFF REPORT AS MODIFIED

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  C. RECREATION FEE REVIEW

  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA provided a brief overview per the
  agenda material.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if the current sports leagues will be refunded due to the
  COVID-19 situation. ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER (ACM) DAVIS refunds have not
  been confirmed since leagues may opt to play during the summer if fields open back
  up in June to organized recreation.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA to:

  APPROVE RECREATION FEES AS PRESENTED BY STAFF.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA REQUESTED A ROLL CALL:

  AYES: Persichina, Pope, Ciarolla, Bain, McCormick, Retz, & Romanelli
  NAYES: None
  ABSENT : None

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  D. SPECIAL EVENTS PERMIT FEE REVIEW

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided a brief overview
  per the agenda material.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked about traffic control. ACM DAVIS stated that events
  under the Temporary Use Permit (TUP) process have traffic control guidelines due to
  events that may take place on the street and this process was applied to the
  Community Services Department due to special events such as the Portuguese Bend
  Horse Show which takes place on City property that also require traffic control. City
  staff would determine if a traffic review would be needed. If a traffic plan is required
  then the cost would be borne by the organizer. CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if the
  Portuguese Bend Horse Show was the only event that required traffic control.
  SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH noted the Music Festival and Beer and Wine
  Festival also used bussing to and from Ernie Howlett Park, which required traffic

DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
MAY 18, 2020
   control. ACM DAVIS noted some school races use the TUP of $600 to use the Park
  and that the more cost-effective special event fee structure would be better for such
  non-profit organizations. The PV Street Fair also uses the TUP which is waived by
  the City but using the Special Event Fees will better streamline this process.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the events that would subject to Special
  Event Fees were contacted. Staff responded that several event organizers were
  contacted and agreed with the fee changes. SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted the
  fees are comparable or less expensive than the surrounding Cities’ special event fees.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  CIAROLLA to:

  APPROVE SPECIAL EVENTS PERMIT FEES PRESENTED BY STAFF.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA REQUESTED A ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES: Persichina, Pope, Ciarolla, Bain, McCormick, Retz, & Romanelli
  NAYES: None
  ABSENT : None

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  7.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION

  A.  2020 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE DIRECTOR AGREEMENT

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided a brief overview per
  the agenda material.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the event were to take place in the Fall, if City staff would
  be able to run the event without the Race Director. SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO
  answered that staff would be able to run the event without the Director with the
  understanding that attendance may be lower due to the COVID 19 situation.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if staff could provide the same services without the use of
  a race director. SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO answered that staff could provide the
  same type of event as before. SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that sponsorship
  which was previously provided by the Director can be contacted by City staff instead.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the City could run the event at a smaller capacity, if it
  would be possible to run a larger event without the Director if there is dissatisfaction with
  his service. ACM DAVIS responded that a debriefing would be held after this year’s event
  to allow the Commission to have that discussion. CHAIR PERSICHINA noted that prior
  to hiring a race Director the City organized the event by itself with staff and noted it was
  run well in the past. The Director’s main role was to increase participation and
  sponsorship. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that incentives could be added to a

DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
MAY 18, 2020
   future agreement as the City would be coming off of lower projected participation numbers
  for 2020.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA noted that the date of the event should be kept and that a deadline
  be placed in case the City needs to postpone the race. ACM DAVIS noted that more
  guidance on public gatherings may be provided in June and that staff should still have
  time to organize a race within that time.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI notified staff that Walt Ordway of the HAM Radio
  operators will need to be contacted along with other key players of the race of the status
  of the event. SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO responded that all Walt Ordway will be kept
  abreast of the situation as more information comes out.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted the cancellation clause still allows the Director to cancel
  within 30 days of the event with $2,000 and there is no restriction on his ability to cancel.
  This should be an issue to be looked at for the 2021 agreement. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI noted an incentive clause should also be added to increase participation.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK
  to:

  ACCEPT STAFF REPORT AS RECEIVED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA received and filed.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A. ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted that Dapplegray Park has a loose post near the
  dressage ring between E and A. SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH noted the post
  will be looked at tomorrow.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noticed the barbeque in the grass bowl area at Ernie
  Howlett needed to be replaced. SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH noted a
  replacement will be installed.

  9.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
MAY 18, 2020
   ACM DAVIS reported that City Hall has reopened with precautions for staff and the public
  such as encouraging appointments and asking the public to wear face covering when
  entering the building. The lobby has been limited to one person or household at a time
  with an outdoor waiting area. Items such as plans will be kept in quarantine from staff for
  one to two days in order to limit spread of COVID-19. Retail shops have been reopened
  as well under the County’s reopening plan under specific guidelines. Staff will continue
  working with the Chamber of Commerce, City Council, and Mayor to provide our local
  businesses support. Park facilities such as the tennis courts have reopened on a limited
  basis but other areas such as sports fields remain closed to group gatherings. Sheriff
  have been called to break up any large groups such as pick-up games and have served
  as educators rather than enforcers of the County guidelines.  Hiking trails have been
  opened as well. The playground and basketball court remain closed. Gatherings have
  been cancelled at parks. Staff interaction is being limited by requesting exact change at
  the tennis office or paying with checks. Online and credit card payment is not yet
  implemented at the park. Singles play and social distancing is enforced at the tennis
  courts along with face covering. Hand sanitizing stations will also be set up soon. Tennis
  instructor Bob will also be allowed to host limited tennis lessons with a maximum of two
  people. The Peter Weber Equestrian Center and City horse arenas are also operating
  under the Order’s guidelines. The City is in the early part of Stage Two of the County’s
  Reopening, which limits public gatherings and hope to transition to Stage Three later in
  the Summer per the County’s timeline.

  Angela Horonco a local equestrian asked about the different requirements for horse
  trainers but notified the Commission that she was emailed of the rules. ACM DAVIS
  provided a brief overview of County guidelines for horse facilities.

  B.  SPECIAL EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted the cancellation of the
  June movie night and asked the Commission for guidance on the Tracy Austin Tennis
  Tournament. ACM DAVIS noted movie nights may not be held in July due to current
  guidelines. The tennis tournament could have alternative options such as a tennis clinic
  or modified event in coordination with Tracy Austin. CHAIR PERSICHINA noted contact
  with the Jack Kramer Club will affected. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the
  upcoming tennis tournament will need to be decided on soon and before the race is
  determined. ACM DAVIS noted that the tennis tournament subcommittee can be notified
  of the situation and can provide a recommendation to the Commission at the regularly
  scheduled meeting of June 15th. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI suggested inviting Tracy
  Austin into the subcommittee’s discussions on the event. VICE CHAIR POPE asked if
  there was any discussion on postponing the event to a later date. SUPERVISOR
  MORQUECHO noted that it has not been discussed yet but that moving the date would
  move into other special event dates such as the race and holiday parade.

  C.  MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE (VERBAL REPORT)

  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that with the current restrictions on trail riding, only
  four horses in single file at a time can be had on the trail making for a more exclusive
  event. Post-ride gathering may also be restricted as to promote social distancing in

DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
MAY 18, 2020
   accordance to current County guidelines. The ride is suggested to take place on July 4th
  with pre-packaged meals so as to forgo the use of the Scout Breakfast aspect of the event.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested having food at the ride would promote social gathering.
  She added that if the lock-down is extended for another 90 days, the July 4th date of the
  event would not be suitable. ACM DAVIS responded that the County plans on staggered
  restrictions over time and that gatherings may be limited to ten or less. As a result, there
  may be less restrictions after the July 4th date.
  D.  YMCA SUMMER SWIMMING PROGRAM (VERBAL REPORT)
  ACM DAVIS noted that swimming pools are unlikely to be open this summer due to the
  COVID-19 situation so the summer swim program does not look like it will be held.
  E.  ACADEMY HILL HOA REQUEST (VERBAL REPORT)
  SUPERINTENDENT GOLDSMITH notified the Commission of the eucalyptus tree which
  will be replaced by the HOA at the entry point adjacent to Palos Verdes Drive North, which
  ACM DAVIS noted is City property but is maintained by the unincorporated HOA. The
  HOA will share its landscape design for the median with the Commission when it is
  prepared.
  F.  PROPOSED PARK TOURS SCHEDULE
  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided a brief overview per
  the agenda material. Commissioners agreed with the schedule.
  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION
  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 28, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF MAY 12, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PVPLC ANNUAL REPORT

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the status of Taber Grove. ACM DAVIS
  responded that it will be added to a future agenda in the Fall after the park tours. More
  clarification is needed in regards to the work needed on the City property line for phase
  one of the project.

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR POPE to,

DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
MAY 18, 2020
   ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 8:38 PM TO AN ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON JUNE 15, 2020 AT 7:00 P.M. IN THE ZOOM CHAT
  FORMAT.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,
